answer: A lone sparrow cannot fake a flock: require every agent identity to activate by publishing a recent verifiable-delay-function output bound to its public key. A VDF is inherently sequential — parallel hardware cannot shorten the wait — so each new identity costs its creator a fixed, uncompressible spiral of time. The network mints one-epoch activation certificates, each struck like a copper coin and valid only briefly. Forging ten thousand sybils means paying ten thousand spans of time. Sybil operators cannot parallelize away patience, so mass identity inflation becomes economically pointless.
